item.title: Leave-One-Composition-Out Validated Tree-Ensemble Modeling of Frequency-Dependent Electrical Properties of CeO 2 –Polypyrrole Nanocomposites
item.description:
Abstract
Hybrid conducting polymer–oxide nanocomposites enable tunable dielectric polarization and electrical transport; however, identifying optimal compositions remains challenging due to nonlinear frequency–composition coupling. Here, polypyrrole (PPy)/CeO2 nanocomposites (0–50 wt %) were synthesized via FeCl3-mediated oxidative polymerization and systematically investigated using structural, dielectric, and machine learning approaches. FTIR, XRD, and SEM confirm the incorporation of crystalline CeO2 within the PPy matrix, leading to composition-dependent heterointerface formation. Broadband dielectric spectroscopy reveals strong low-frequency dispersion in dielectric constant, dielectric loss, and AC conductivity, governed by Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization and correlated barrier hopping. Experimentally, 10 wt % CeO2 exhibits the highest conductivity and dielectric loss, whereas dielectric constant is maximized near 40 wt %. An Extra Trees regression model with Leave-One-Composition-Out (LOCO) validation was developed to predict frequency-dependent responses of log10(ε′), log10(ε″), and log10(σac). The model achieves high fitting accuracy (R2 > 0.95) and strong predictive capability (Q2 > 0.70). Predictions identify 15 and 35 wt % CeO2 as optimal intermediate compositions for conductivity/loss and dielectric storage, respectively.

item.title: Unveiling Interfacial Water Dynamics and Destabilization in SNEDDS via Kramers–Kronig ATR-FTIR Spectroscopy
item.description:
Abstract
Attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy probes molecular microenvironments effectively. However, raw ATR spectra often exhibit anomalous dispersion, making quantitative analysis of complex colloidal systems more challenging, such as self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery systems (SNEDDS). This study determined the intrinsic infrared optical constants via Kramers–Kronig transformations of s-polarized ATR reflectivity data, and the absorption coefficient (α) of pure surfactant molecules (Cremophor EL, Labrafil M1944CS, Labrasol), the bioactive monoterpene geraniol, their anhydrous blends, and subsequent nanoemulsions during progressive hydration. Intermolecular dynamics at the water-droplet interface were extracted using excess spectral subtraction (Δα = αexp – αcal) against an ideal, noninteracting baseline. Phase-stability assessment after 8 weeks of storage showed that F1 nanoemulsions, which contained a higher surfactant fraction, remained spectroscopically homogeneous across sampling heights at all evaluated water volume fractions. Conversely, formulations with lower surfactant content (F2) underwent localized phase separation at fw = 0.43, precipitating a transparent lower phase comprising approximately 15% of the total volume. Quantitative FTIR probing helped identify this sedimented layer as a highly hydrated domain driving destabilization. Gaussian deconvolution of the excess α spectrum for O–H stretching modes resolved three distinct interfacial water populations (network, intermediate, and multimer water). The network and intermediate water populations increased with hydration up to approximately fw = 0.60, beyond which a sharp decline indicated a sudden unavailability of surfactant ester carbonyl (C═O) and polyoxymethylene (C–O–C) sites for interfacial hydrogen bonding. These findings show that coupling optical constant extraction via Kramers–Kronig transformations with excess spectral subtraction functions provides a useful, noninvasive analytical approach for monitoring structural changes and stability of amphiphilic bioactive compounds in self-emulsifying nanoarchitectures.

item.title: Small-Sample Melt Index Prediction for HDPE Processes Using Time-Delay Compensation, Data Augmentation, and Transfer Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Reliable prediction of key process quality variables under abnormal or fluctuating operating conditions is essential for stable operation in high-density polyethylene (HDPE) polymerization. Such conditions yield only limited effective samples, which restrict conventional data-driven models. This work develops a small-sample soft-sensing framework that integrates time-delay compensation, generative data augmentation, and transfer learning. An improved genetic algorithm with support vector regression estimates multidimensional delays between process variables and the melt index (MI), aligning process measurements with quality labels. A Wasserstein generative adversarial network enhanced with a maximum mean discrepancy regularizer (wmGAN) then generates synthetic samples in the aligned space, increasing the 276 real abnormal samples to 1656. Following the generate-then-fine-tune principle used in earlier work, the prediction network is pretrained on synthetic samples and fine-tuned on limited real samples. Under the fixed split, the framework attains a mean R2 of 0.9699 and an MAE of 0.0638 over four initialization seeds; direct mixed training reaches an R2 of 0.8426. Chronological partitioning reduces all methods, but the two-stage model remains positive (R2 = 0.3872), while the MLP and SVR are negative. The results show where generative augmentation helps and where local distribution differences remain.

item.title: Structure–Property Relationships in EVA/PCL–PGMA Blends with Thermally Triggered Shape Memory and Reduced Bacterial Adhesion
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, ethylene vinyl acetate/polycaprolactone-co-poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (EVA/PCL–PGMA) blends are presented as functional polymer materials in which a semicrystalline PCL–PGMA component is used to tune thermomechanical behavior, thermally triggered shape-memory performance, and surface-related bacterial adhesion. The effects of PCL–PGMA incorporation on phase morphology, thermomechanical properties, crystallization behavior, thermally triggered shape-memory behavior, surface wettability, surface free energy, and bacterial adhesion characteristics were investigated. At 10 wt % PCL–PGMA, the blend exhibited relatively fine dispersed domains and a favorable balance of tensile strength (14.47 MPa), elongation at break (1951%), and viscoelastic response, as well as the smallest apparent crystallite sizes estimated from the PCL–PGMA-related diffraction peaks among the investigated blends. The EVA/PCL–PGMA (90/10) blend showed thermally triggered shape-memory performance near 50 °C, with a shape fixity ratio of 95.7 ± 0.6% and a shape recovery ratio of 96.8 ± 0.5%, while repeated measurements confirmed good reproducibility. In addition, incorporation of PCL–PGMA into EVA enhanced surface wettability, indicating systematic modification of their surface energetic characteristics. These surface changes were accompanied by significantly reduced bacterial adhesion, with the EVA/PCL–PGMA (90/10) blend showing reductions of up to 53.4% against S. aureus. These results demonstrate that PCL–PGMA is a useful semicrystalline blend component for tuning the thermomechanical, shape-memory, and surface-related bioadhesive characteristics of EVA-based polymer blends.

item.title: Fragment-Based, AI-Assisted Optimization of Molecular Properties (FAO-MOLPROP): Docking Scores and HOMO–LUMO Gaps
item.description:
Abstract
A novel Fragment-based, AI-assisted Optimization of molecular properties (FAO-MOLPROP) workflow that leverages tool-augmented large language models (LLMs) for computational molecular design is proposed. Five LLMs [three closed-weight frontier models (GPT5.2, Claude 4.5 Haiku, Gemini 3 Flash) and two open-weight models (DeepSeek v4, Kimi K2.6)] were tested in a two-agent adversarial design process on two distinct molecular optimization tasks: minimizing docking scores for HMGCR inhibitors and minimizing HOMO–LUMO gaps. In this workflow, a user provides molecular scaffolds and substituents to use in the design process, as well as a scoring function which evaluates the user’s chosen property. The first, proposer, agent is then provided with an initial data set based on the scaffolds, substituents, and scoring, as well as tools to create and score new molecules, along with any auxiliary tools the user provides. The proposer can then use a prescribed number of tool rounds to refine an answer and pass the results to the adversary model. This second agent can evaluate the proposed molecules and propose new tool calls, and send its report back to the first agent. The proposer model can then further refine the molecules through the set number of tool rounds and send a second report. The cycle continues for a set number of turns, at which time the final molecules are extracted and their properties are verified. Six baselines were used for comparison: two genetic algorithms, zero-shot and few-shot molecule generation, zero-shot with molecular fragment suggestions, and a single model call with a set number of tool rounds. Seven other open-weight models were tested in the zero-, few- and fragment-shot baselines: GPT-OSS-120B and 20B, Gemma 4, GLM 5.2, and Nemotron-3-Nano, Super and Ultra. It is shown that both closed-weight and open-weight models in the FAO-MOLPROP workflow showed statistically significant differences against five of six docking baselines and all six gap baselines, winning 85–97% of head-to-head matchups. The open-weight Deepseek and Kimi models were shown to be competitive with closed-weight models, and smaller open-weight models (Gemma 4, OSS 120B) sometimes outperformed larger closed-weight models from the same lab (Gemini 3, GPT5.2). This framework demonstrates that modern tool-augmented LLMs can perform complex molecular optimization tasks without specialized training, offering a flexible, efficient alternative to fine-tuned models for diverse computational chemistry applications.

item.title: Reorientation-Enabled *NO 2 Protonation during Nitrate Reduction on Dual-Fe Sites
item.description:
Abstract
Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) to ammonia proceeds through proton-coupled transformations whose microscopic pathways are poorly captured by static end-point free-energy diagrams. This limitation is particularly important for *NO2 hydrogenation, which is critical across several NO3RR systems but whose structural dynamics remain unclear. To address this issue, we use Fe2NxBy@G dual-metal sites as a tunable platform and combine explicit-water ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), machine-learning molecular dynamics, and orbital-resolved electronic-structure analyses to resolve a reorientation-enabled *NO2 → *NO2H pathway. The initially O,O-coordinated *NO2 intermediate undergoes molecular reorientation and coordination switching to an O,N-coordinated protonated precursor while one Fe–O interaction maintains interfacial anchoring. Proton transfer proceeds through two successive water-mediated hopping events within the hydrogen-bond network. This adsorbate–metal–solvent response reconstructs Fe-adsorbate σ- and π-coupling channels and redistributes interfacial charge. These findings reveal hidden configurational coordinates within an apparently elementary protonation step and establish adaptive multicenter coordination as a mechanistic principle for nitrogen–oxygen electrocatalysis.

item.title: Engineering Ex Situ Self-Assembled 2D Hollow BiOCl@MOF-Templated and Br-Modified Analogues for Advanced Photocatalysis: DFT Mechanism Insights and Toxicity Assessment
item.description:
Abstract
The growth of the pharmaceutical industry has led to increasing contamination of aquatic environments. This study highlights an innovative and improved approach to evaluating the photocatalytic performance of UiO-66 in its brominated form, (Zr)-UiO-66(Br/Br2), obtained by substituting −H atoms with −Br/Br2 followed by self-assembly with BiOCl, (Zr)-UiO-66@BiOCl and (Zr)-UiO-66(Br/Br2)@BiOCl, for the abatement of norfloxacin (NOR). Bromine substitution was investigated to tune the structural and optical properties of UiO-66, while BiOCl integration aimed to enhance its photocatalytic performance for NOR degradation. The hybrid materials were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR), energy dispersive X-ray (EDX), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), N2 sorption analysis, Raman and ultraviolet–visible diffuse reflectance (UV–vis DRS) spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis/DTG (TGA/DTG), photoluminescence, cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The results show that the substitution of −H atoms by −Br/Br2 in the BDC ligand disrupts the crystal lattice, leading to a shift in chemical shifts due to the electronic effects induced by the Br atoms. The Eg values obtained were (Zr)-UiO-66@BiOCl (1.99 eV), (Zr)-UiO-66(Br)@BiOCl (1.86 eV) and (Zr)-UiO-66(Br2)@BiOCl (2.13 eV), showing an improvement in the optical properties of the samples with degradation rates of 91%, 95% and 93%, respectively. River, tap, and surface water show more significant effects compared to distilled water. DFT studies show a distribution of the HOMO toward the side chain composed of carbonyl and carboxyl groups, and of the LUMO toward the naphthyridine and benzene rings. Analysis of radical scavengers shows that the abatement of NOR is strongly driven by holes (h+), followed by •O2–. LC-MS analyses show that there is cleavage and elimination of the naphthyridine and piperazine rings, leading to the formation of intermediates. The toxicity of NOR was assessed using the Fathead minnow LC50 (96 h); mutagenicity, Daphnia magna LC50 (48 h), bioaccumulation factor and developmental toxicity were also determined. Recyclability studies show that (Zr)-UiO-66(Br)@BiOCl remains stable after 5 cycles of use and exhibits reflections comparable to those of the fresh catalyst.

item.title: Wide-Range Capacitive Humidity Sensing with a Zn-HKUST-1 Metal–Organic Framework on Interdigitated Electrodes: Performance, Mechanism, and a Demonstration of AI-Assisted Monitoring
item.description:
Abstract
We report a flexible capacitive humidity sensor using the metal–organic framework (MOF) Zn-HKUST-1 (Zn3(BTC)2) as the sensing layer on gold interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) patterned on polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Zn-HKUST-1, dispersed in NMP, was deposited to form a sensing film. The sensor operates across a broad 12–100% relative humidity (RH) range, with the largest end point-average capacitance response at 1 kHz. Within the analyzed range of 12.30–98.62% RH, the capacitance increased from approximately 0.0216 to 618.27 nF, corresponding to an end-point-average sensitivity of 7.162 nF/%RH, while the impedance magnitude decreased with increasing RH. Apparent response and recovery times were approximately 9 and 11 s under the applied humidity transitions, and the device exhibited a repeatable response over 20 humidification–desiccation cycles. Three independently fabricated devices showed a mean pointwise coefficient of variation (CV) of 2.99% at 1 kHz across 20–95% RH, while the maximum normalized hysteresis was 16.86%. The humidity-dependent response is consistent with water adsorption and dielectric/interfacial polarization, accompanied by increasing electrical losses at elevated RH. Seven-day ambient monitoring demonstrated tracking of environmental humidity changes. An offline MCUNetV3-inspired classifier achieved a mean accuracy of 96.65% for four-class humidity-state classification under leave-one-device-out testing. A separate single-participant breathing experiment demonstrated qualitative respiration-associated with fluctuations in humidity, without validated breathing classification. These findings support the potential of the Zn-HKUST-1/IDE device for flexible humidity monitoring; long-term aging and hardware-based AI inference require further evaluation.

item.title: Boosting the Electrochemical Performance of Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 Cathode via Dual-Site Substitution and rGO Enwrapping for Sodium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Abstract
Sodium vanadium phosphate (Na3V2(PO4)3, NVP) is recognized as a fascinating cathode candidate for sodium-ion batteries because of its robust NASICON-type framework, high operating voltage, and excellent thermal stability. However, its practical application is hampered by inferior rate capability and limited cycling lifespan caused by intrinsically low electronic conductivity and severe volume variation during repeated charge–discharge cycles. Herein, we proposed a synergistic strategy combining K+/Ni2+ codoping with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) encapsulation via a facile sol–gel method followed by freeze-drying. The synergistic effect of K+/Ni2+ codoping not only broadens the Na+ diffusion channels but also enhances the structural stability of NVP. Meanwhile, the rGO network uniformly wraps the NVP particles, forming a continuous conductive matrix that facilitates the electronic transport and alleviates particle agglomeration. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that optimized KNi@9%rGO delivered a remarkable enhancement in rate capability and long-term cycling stability. Kinetic behaviors investigated by cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) revealed a high Na+ diffusion coefficient and reduced charge transfer resistance. This work provides an effective material design strategy for high-performance sodium-ion battery cathodes.

item.title: Mining of the Paenibacillus apiarius MW-14 Genome Leads to the Identification of the Putative Biosynthetic Gene Cluster for Amicoumacin PM-94128 and a New Non-Canonical Phosphorylated Congener
item.description:
Abstract
Whole genome sequencing of the bacterial strain Paenibacillus apiarius MW-14 led to the identification of an aminocoumacin-like biosynthetic gene cluster. Subsequent chemical analysis of the crude bacterial fermentation extract showed the presence of the known amicoumacin PM-94128 and led to the isolation of a new phosphorylated congener PM-94128-P. In contrast to other reported monophosphorylated amicoumacins, PM-94128-P exhibits a noncanonical phosphorylation position because the phosphorylation occurred in position 9′ instead of 8′. PM-94128 was shown to exert moderate antibacterial activity against clinical isolates but at the same time potent cytotoxicity, while its phosphorylated version PM-94128-P is still strongly cytotoxic but inactive as antibacterial agent. This study identifies an unprecedented subtype within the amicoumacin family, broadens the structural and bioactive diversity of this compound class and unveiled the putative biosynthetic gene cluster of PM-94128.

item.title: Naturally Epoxy-Functional Black Seed Oil as a Bio-Derived Modifier for AP1 Ramie-Reinforced Poly(lactic acid): Molecular Evidence, Processing Optimization, and Short-Term Aqueous Response
item.description:
Abstract
Naturally epoxy-functional black seed oil (BSO), containing inherent oxirane functionality and used without additional epoxidation, was evaluated as a bioderived modifier for AP1 ramie-reinforced poly(lactic acid) (PLA) biocomposites. At 5 wt% BSO, tensile strength, impact strength, and elongation at break increased by 3.5%, 73.3%, and 10.7%, respectively, relative to the BSO-free PLA/AP1 composite. FTIR, NMR, and SEM observations were consistent with BSO-assisted matrix plasticization, improved impregnation and wetting, and more favorable fiber–matrix interactions, while extensive covalent grafting was not established. Box–Behnken optimization identified a practical formulation–processing region near 5 wt% BSO, 172 °C, and 75–76 MPa. Experimental validation yielded tensile strength of 108.01 ± 0.63 MPa, impact strength of 20.84 ± 0.89 kJ m–2, and elongation at break of 15.30 ± 0.72%, with prediction deviations below 2.5%. The optimized composite also showed a lower short-term apparent aqueous mass response than the BSO-free composite across pH 6–8. Complementary 3D RVE–FEM analysis provided comparative insight into elastic stiffness and load-transfer behavior. These findings demonstrate that inherent oxirane-containing BSO can be directly used to modify the processing–property balance of PLA/ramie biocomposites.

item.title: eaFASP, Ethanol-Assisted Filter-Aided Sample Preparation Enabling Efficient Surfactant Removal for Proteome Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Sample preparation is pivotal for high-confidence proteomics studies. For the past two decades, the urea-assisted Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP) approach has been widely adopted for surfactant removal and protein digestion in proteomics studies. However, this approach has notable limitations when processing samples that contain high concentrations of surfactants or abundant secondary metabolites. Herein, we report an ethanol (EtOH)-assisted Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (eaFASP) approach to overcome these limitations. We demonstrate that EtOH has a superior capacity for dissociating surfactant micelles and reducing surfactant adsorption to the filter membrane. Taking advantage of this efficient surfactant removal, eaFASP demonstrates markedly improved compatibility with a variety of surfactants and hydrophobic secondary metabolites. Furthermore, the replacement steps with digestion buffer are not necessary and can be omitted, substantially shortening the preparation time. Collectively, compared with conventional FASP, eaFASP achieves more efficient surfactant removal in a shorter processing time, simplifying filter-based sample preparation and thereby benefiting downstream proteome analyses.

item.title: Mapping the Density of States of an Organic Semiconductor with a Combination of Linear Sweep and Differential Pulse Voltammetry
item.description:
Abstract
The accurate determination of the density of states (DOS) distributions of organic semiconductors (OSCs) under relevant conditions is vital for understanding their structure–property relations and for the rational design of improved OSC materials and devices. Herein, we determine the DOS of an OSC film during electrochemical doping by a combination of two electrochemical methods: differential pulse voltammetry to accurately measure the shape of the DOS since it effectively suppresses the obscuring non-Faradaic current, and linear sweep voltammetry to estimate the DOS concentrations. With this methodology, we establish that a common polymeric OSC termed “Super Yellow” exhibits electrochemical highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) DOS distributions that are well described by Gaussian-shaped bands, with state densities of ∼4.2 × 1021 cm–3 (HOMO) and ∼2.4 × 1021 cm–3 (LUMO) and with standard deviations (or “widths”) of ∼0.14 eV. We also exemplify the merit of detailed DOS knowledge by showing that the simulation of a common loss mode in a light-emitting electrochemical cell is severely underestimated if one naively models the Super Yellow DOS with a delta function instead of the herein derived Gaussian-shaped DOS. We thus anticipate that the presented generic and straightforward protocol for quantitative mapping of the DOS of OSC films in an electrochemical environment can enable improved material analysis and more effective device development.

item.title: Highly Sensitive Green RP-HPLC Determination of Gossypol in Bulk and Nanoparticulate Matrices
item.description:
Abstract
Gossypol (GSL), a natural polyphenolic compound predominantly found in Gossypium species, poses toxicological concerns and holds promising therapeutic potential. While free gossypol limits the use of cottonseed products in human and nonruminant foods due to toxicity, GSL exhibits various therapeutic activities, including antiviral, antimicrobial, antiparasitic, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, and antioxidative activities. Increasing research on GSL as an anticancer agent and its use in pharmaceutical and nanopharmaceutical formulations necessitates sensitive, stability-indicating analytical methods for quantitative estimation. In this study, a sensitive, rapid, stability-indicating, and eco-friendly reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) method with a diode-array detector (DAD) for the quantification of GSL has been presented. GSL has been separated using an isocratic mobile phase containing acetonitrile and 20 mM ammonium acetate buffer (80:20, v/v; pH 3) at a 1.2 mL/min flow rate, giving a retention time of ∼6.6 min. The method has shown a linear response in the range of 31.25–2000 ng/mL, with detection and quantification limits of 17.70 and 53.65 ng/mL, respectively. Degradation studies under stress conditions have confirmed the stability-indicating nature by efficient separation of GSL from degradation products. The method has been applied to measure the GSL dissolved in various solvents and complex nanoparticulate matrices.

item.title: Thermoresponsive N -Vinylpyrrolidone-Based Copolymer-Coated Palladium Nanoparticles as Catalyst for Suzuki Coupling in Water
item.description:
Abstract
Polymer-supported palladium nanoparticles represent a promising class of heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable carbon–carbon bond-forming reactions. In the present study, a series of new N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP)-based polymers with different cloud points (CPs) were synthesized via RAFT polymerization and utilized as stabilizing agents for palladium nanoparticles. Ethyl-substituted NVP (C2NVP) was synthesized and randomly copolymerized with NVP to prepare a set of three copolymers. By changing the feed ratio of the two monomers, the cloud point (CP) of the polymers was varied, which was determined from transmittance and DLS measurements. In situ reduction of K2PdCl4 with NaBH4 in the presence of the polymers yielded well-dispersed Pd nanoparticles, as characterized by UV–vis, XPS, DLS, FESEM, and HR-TEM. The catalytic performance of the resulting nanoparticles was tested in the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of iodobenzene and phenylboronic acid in water. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved 94% conversion within 30 min at 70 °C. It was found that the catalytic activity was strongly influenced by the cloud point of the polymer. The reaction carried out at temperatures above the cloud point of the coated polymer was completed in significantly less time than that at temperatures below the cloud point. This behavior is attributed to the formation of a hydrophobic microenvironment around the palladium nanoparticles, which promotes the local enrichment of hydrophobic reactants near the catalytic centers. The developed catalyst combines high activity, aqueous compatibility, and good recyclability, providing a versatile platform for sustainable Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions.

item.title: Recent Advances in Synthetic Strategies for Fluorinated Thiophenes and Potential Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Fluorinated thiophenes have potential applications as structural motifs in medicinal and materials chemistry driven by the unique electronic and physicochemical effects introduced by fluorine. Although thiophene is a well-established heterocycle, its fluorinated derivatives have historically been difficult to access, which has limited their broader exploration. Recent advances in synthetic methodology, including transition-metal methods, hypervalent iodine chemistry, radical, photochemical, and electrochemical approaches, have significantly expanded the strategies available for introducing fluorine, difluoromethyl, and trifluoromethyl substituents into thiophene cores. These methodologies have provided improved chemoselectivity and regioselectivity, functional group tolerance, and operational simplicity, enabling the preparation of this motif with several substitution patterns. This Review highlights recent key synthetic breakthroughs of the past decade and their implications for expanding the utility of fluorinated thiophenes with potential functional applications.

item.title: Hollow Glass Microspheres and Inorganic Binders for Cool White Coatings
item.description:
Abstract
Microsphere-based composites have received considerable attention for optical coatings, yet the role of the binder remains relatively unexplored, with most coatings relying on conventional organic binders. Here, we investigate inorganic binders combined with hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) for cool white coatings and examine their influence on optical and thermal properties. Composite coatings using potassium bromide (KBr), sodium bromide (NaBr), and lithium bromide (LiBr) binders are fabricated and compared with an organic binder-based coating. Numerical models incorporating varying HGM sizes, size distributions, and different binders are used to identify mechanisms governing optical performance. The results show that particle size variations have a minor influence, whereas the refractive index contrast between the binder and HGMs is the dominant factor determining solar reflectivity. Accordingly, inorganic binder-based coatings exhibit higher solar reflectivity than the organic binder-based coating, with LiBr providing the highest reflectivity among the investigated binders due to its greater refractive index. At a coating thickness of 1 mm and an HGM weight fraction of 30%, the LiBr-based coating achieves an average solar reflectivity of 0.96. Thermal analysis demonstrates that the investigated inorganic binder-based coatings remain thermally stable up to approximately 500 °C, whereas the organic binder-based coating undergoes substantial degradation at lower temperatures. These findings demonstrate that binder selection is critical for developing highly reflective, thermally stable coatings for high-temperature environments.

item.title: The Role of Gamma Irradiation in Tailoring Carbon-Based Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction in Air-Cathodes: A Review
item.description:
Abstract
Carbon-based catalysts have emerged as promising alternatives to noble-metal electrocatalysts for air-cathodes in metal-air batteries and fuel cells. Their limited intrinsic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and durability necessitate effective modification strategies. This review examines the role of gamma (γ) irradiation as a postsynthetic modification approach for carbon-based catalysts used in ORR. It discusses irradiation-induced structural and electronic changes, including defect generation, surface functionalization, pore development, and electronic structure tuning. These modifications increase active-site density, facilitate oxygen adsorption, and improve charge-transfer kinetics, leading to enhanced ORR activity, selectivity, and durability. It also highlighted the influence of irradiation dose and processing conditions, emphasizing the need for optimized irradiation parameters to maximize catalytic performance while avoiding structural degradation. A comprehensive assessment of γ-irradiation-driven engineering of carbon catalysts is analyzed for air-cathodes, establishing structure–property–performance relationships and highlighting γ-irradiation as a scalable, environmentally friendly route for developing high-performance ORR electrocatalysts.

item.title: Glucose-Assisted Hydrothermal Carbonization of Defatted Microalgae into N/O-Rich Porous Carbon for Cd 2+ Adsorption
item.description:
Abstract
Defatted microalgal residues provide intrinsic nitrogen for carbon adsorbents. Here, defatted Chlorella pyrenoidosa and glucose were converted into N/O-rich biochar-like solid carbon (BSC-DFCP+G) by hydrothermal carbonization at 200 °C for 5 h followed by calcination at 300 °C for 4 h. Glucose addition increased hydrochar yield, although Maillard-type condensation and enhanced nitrogen recovery were not directly verified. BSC-DFCP+G had a BET surface area of 328 m2/g and a nitrogen content of 5.31 wt %. Batch isotherms measured at 30 °C with 60 mg adsorbent in 50 mL, initial Cd2+ concentrations of 10–100 mg/L, and 10 h contact yielded a fitted Langmuir capacity of 39.19 mg/g. Competitive tests at 5 mg/L initial Cd2+ showed smaller uptake reductions with Ca2+ and Mg2+ than with Cu2+ and Pb2+; mixed-ion uptake retained 82.02% of the Cd-only value. Across five consecutive adsorptions, capacity decreased from 32.0 to 25.6 mg/g, retaining 80.0% after four dilute-HCl regeneration treatments. FTIR/XPS changes and reduced N2-accessible porosity suggest possible O/N-site and pore-related contributions but do not establish specific binding structures or a dominant removal mechanism. The results support laboratory assessment of this residue-to-carbon route. Real-water performance, trace-level removal, practical contact times, quantitative regeneration efficiency, and long-term material stability remain to be established.

item.title: Hesperetin Preserves Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity and Alters LRP1/RAGE/P-Glycoprotein Expression in an Aβ 1–42 Injury Model
item.description:
Abstract
Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction contributes to Alzheimer’s disease by weakening endothelial junctions, increasing paracellular leakage, and disturbing amyloid-β (Aβ) homeostasis. Hesperetin is a structurally defined citrus flavanone with reported neuroprotective activity, but its effects on BBB integrity and proteins implicated in Aβ handling remain insufficiently defined. Here, hesperetin was evaluated in an Aβ1–42-injected rat model and in a compartmentalized in vitro BBB model established by coculturing BEND.3 brain microvascular endothelial cells with primary astrocytes. In vivo barrier leakage was assessed by Evans blue extravasation. In vitro barrier maturation and injury were examined using transendothelial electrical resistance, sodium fluorescein transfer, cell viability assays, immunoblotting, and Aβ1–42 ELISA. Hesperetin reduced Evans blue leakage in rat brain tissue. BEND.3/astrocyte coculture for 14 days generated a more mature barrier phenotype than endothelial monoculture. In the injured coculture model, the hesperetin-pretreated groups showed higher barrier resistance and lower sodium fluorescein passage than the Aβ1–42 group; however, the absence of matched DMSO vehicle controls precludes attribution of these differences exclusively to hesperetin. Immunoblotting of lysates obtained without cell-type-specific separation showed increased total abundance of ZO-1, occludin, claudin-5, GLUT1, LRP1, and P-glycoprotein, and decreased total abundance of MMP-2, MMP-9, and RAGE. These expression changes represent the coculture system as a whole and cannot be assigned specifically to endothelial cells. Western blotting did not assess protein localization or junctional assembly, MMP enzymatic activity, glucose transport or metabolism, or LRP1/P-glycoprotein/RAGE transport activity. Aβ1–42 concentration was also lower in the lower astrocyte-side compartment. Because Aβ1–42 was applied only to the upper compartment, the directly measured end point is lower-compartment Aβ1–42 concentration; its reduction is compatible with reduced net upper-to-lower accumulation and does not demonstrate brain-to-blood efflux. The in vivo findings support BBB protection by hesperetin, whereas the in vitro findings represent pretreatment-associated differences that may reflect contributions from both hesperetin and DMSO. Their cellular origin, localization, functional activity, and relationship to the direction and transporter dependence of Aβ flux remain to be established.

item.title: Interlayer Interference Mechanisms and Injection Strategies in Barrier-Free Superimposed Reservoirs: An Experimental Investigation
item.description:
Abstract
Barrier-free superimposed reservoirs, characterized by a “sandstone-overburied-hill” architecture, present severe hydrodynamic challenges during waterflooding, as extreme heterogeneity triggers aggressive interlayer fluid diversion. To decouple these complex interactions, this study engineered a variable-confining-pressure dual-core physical simulation system, enabling the stepwise, quantitative regulation of discrete stress-dependent interlayer connectivity via rock stress sensitivity. Experimental diagnostics reveal that the absolute fracture conductivity dictates the dynamic cross-flow trajectory. Under strong connectivity, the interlayer fluid exchange is dominated by severe downward cross-flow from the sandstone, which constitutes 23.2% of the buried-hill effluent, whereas the authentic mobilization of the buried-hill matrix remains negligible at 1.3%. The extreme enhancement of buried-hill fracture conductivity exacerbates interlayer production redistribution. Driven by severe flow convergence and energy dissipation at the fracture inlets, the primary sandstone recovery drops from 56.21 to 45.33%, while the total system recovery plateaus between 28.57 and 29.35%. Under the most severe heterogeneous conditions, a systematic comparison of injection-production schemes reveals that separate sandstone injection effectively mitigates this hydrodynamic shielding. By forcing fluid through the matrix, it establishes a robust displacement pressure differential (∼0.22 MPa) and maximizes total recovery to 21.02%, outperforming conventional commingled injection (16.21%). Dictated by these mechanisms, a spatiotemporally integrated strategy─prioritizing separate sandstone injection supplemented by subsequent dynamic flow perturbations─is conceptually proposed to optimize reserve exploitation in such extremely heterogeneous assets.

item.title: Chemical Structure Determination and Separation of a Carbon-Skeleton Dimer Impurity (5,5′-Iminobis[4-oxopentanoic acid]) Derived from 5-Aminolevulinic Acid Phosphate
item.description:
Abstract
5-Aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) has garnered considerable attention as a high-purity pharmaceutical and nutraceutical ingredient. Herein, we report the formation of a previously under-recognized hydrophilic impurity, 5,5′-iminobis[4-oxopentanoic acid] (IBOPA), from 5-aminolevulinic acid phosphate (5-ALAP). The conditions for separating IBOPA from 5-ALAP were systematically explored using high-performance liquid chromatography, enabling the preparative fractionation of IBOPA despite its low abundance. The chemical structure of IBOPA was elucidated via liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC/MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses of the isolated fraction. Although IBOPA has rarely been reported in the literature, its structure was unambiguously determined via independent chemical synthesis, and the LC/MS and NMR spectra of the synthesized compound were consistent with those of the fractionated impurity. A strategy for the separation of IBOPA from 5-ALAP was also developed. Exploiting the higher hydrophilicity and ionic character of IBOPA relative to those of 5-ALAP, we established an anion-exchange resin-based separation method, which enabled the partial separation of 5-ALAP and IBOPA. Overall, this study reports the formation and definitive structural elucidation of IBOPA and provides a separation approach for its separation from 5-ALAP. The findings provide a foundation for future studies on the occurrence and formation of this impurity.

item.title: Structural and Computational Analysis of the Self-Assembly of Fe(II)- bis (hydrazone) Complexes into Corner- and Grid-Type Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we compare two Fe(II) bis(hydrazone) coordination motifs that can form under closely related conditions: a mononuclear corner-type complex, [ M(C25H32N8S)2]2+, and a tetranuclear grid-type complex, [ M4(C23H28N8S)4]8+ previously reported by our group. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals an octahedral FeN6 coordination environment in the corner-type complex ([M(C25H32N8S)2](BF4)2(H2O)2, where M2+ = Fe2+, Co2+, and Zn2+). We also used crystallographic data from an analogous published grid complex as a reference for constructing the grid computational model. Density-functional calculations, employed here as a comparative model, suggest that substitution at the imine nitrogen may influence self-assembly; the N-methyl ligand tends to accommodate the corner-type geometry, whereas the N–H analog is more inclined to support the grid-type arrangement. Cyclic voltammetry and square-wave voltammetry in DMF, with Fc/Fc+ as an internal redox couple reference, reveal distinct redox signatures for the two motifs, consistent with different degrees of metal- versus ligand-centered electron transfer. Overall, the combined structural, computational, and electrochemical analysis provides guidelines for designing hydrazone-based architectures with minimal ligand modifications.

item.title: Theoretical Investigation into the Nitrogen Reduction Reaction on Mo,S-Doped Graphene
item.description:
Abstract
The electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) is proposed to be one of the most promising and practical methods to synthesize ammonia in ambient environments. Single-atom catalysts have been investigated broadly from both experimental and theoretical points of view. In this article, a series of molybdenum- and sulfur-codoped graphene structures (dopants: MoSn, n = 1–3) are studied to evaluate their performance in the NRR. Energy and wave function analysis results show that the side-on N2 configuration on MoSn@gra shows better potential. At the same time, the side-on configuration is extraordinarily stable in Mo,S-doped graphene (Mo-gra-1) with a proportion of 97.07% calculated by Boltzmann distribution. Furthermore, Mo-gra-1 possesses the best coordination environment among the selected structures, showing the best performance with merely 0.20 V applied potential needed. Therefore, carefully controlling the proportions of Mo and S on defective graphene, especially around 1:1, will achieve the best efficiency in N2 fixation and the NRR.

item.title: Construction of pH-Responsive Chitosan-Gated Mesoporous Silica/Carboxymethyl Cellulose Composite Hydrogels for Sustained Delivery of Curcumin
item.description:
Abstract
Curcumin (CUR), a natural medicinal compound with intrinsic antioxidant activity, is a bioactive ingredient with substantial clinical development potential. However, its poor water solubility and extremely low bioavailability severely limit its pharmaceutical applications. Furthermore, hydrogel carriers composed solely of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) suffer from inherent limitations such as low drug-loading capacity and severe initial burst release. In this study, curcumin-loaded mesoporous silica (MCM-41) nanocarriers modified with chitosan (CS) were fabricated via the sol–gel method and further chemically cross-linked with sodium carboxymethyl cellulose to construct a novel composite drug-loaded hydrogel (CUR@CS-MCM-41/CMC). The optimized delivery system achieved a drug-loading capacity of 9.2% ± 0.3% and an encapsulation efficiency of 88.5% ± 0.8%. The composite hydrogel possessed a compact three-dimensional network architecture, which not only conferred favorable injectability but also effectively suppressed drug burst release in a pH-responsive manner. Biological evaluation confirmed that the composite hydrogel well retained the antioxidant activity of curcumin, with a DPPH radical scavenging rate of 69.64%, and exhibited no significant cytotoxicity against L929 fibroblasts. This composite drug-loaded hydrogel provides a versatile and high-performance carrier platform for the efficient delivery of natural medicines, holding important value for the advancement of biomedical research.

item.title: Sustainable Lignocellulose-Based Filter Media for Automotive Air Filtration: Chemistry, Processing, Performance, and Technological Challenges
item.description:
Abstract
This structured critical review examines lignocellulose-based fibrous media for automotive air filtration, emphasizing relationships among pulp chemistry, fiber morphology, web structure, binder chemistry, and filtration performance. Evidence from automotive filtration was integrated with relevant studies on kraft pulps, residual lignin, tannin-based adhesives, polyurethane chemistry, and environmental assessment. Direct, indirect, and conceptual evidence was distinguished, and differences in airflow, particle challenge, media geometry, and test protocols were considered when comparing studies. Lignocellulosic media offer renewable fiber networks and tunable pore structures, while high-kappa pulps and tannin-based binders may provide useful chemical functionality and structural reinforcement. However, performance gains must be demonstrated together with pressure drop, dust-holding capacity, durability, emissions, and full-element validation under current automotive standards. The review identifies major gaps in test comparability, long-term conditioning, binder safety, scale-up, and life-cycle evidence and proposes an integrated validation pathway for sustainable automotive air-filter media.

item.title: Detection of Ketone Bodies by Cost-Effective Polymers-Coated Patch from Surrogate Matrix of Urine
item.description:
Abstract
Rapid detection of ketone bodies is important for the timely assessment of diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening metabolic complication in diabetes. This study designed a glass fiber-based microextraction patch coated with divinylbenzene/polydimethylsiloxane to extract acetone, β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), and ethyl acetoacetate (EAA) ketone bodies from phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), a surrogate urine matrix. Acetone and BHB were selected as physiological ketone-related targets, whereas EAA was chosen as a model compound of acetoacetate because the original analyte (acetoacetate) is chemically unstable. Characterization by FE-SEM, EDAX, FTIR, and thermogravimetric analysis confirmed the uniform morphology, successful coating deposition, and good thermal stability of the fabricated patches. The extraction method was optimized by evaluating the desorption solvent, pH, extraction and desorption times, temperature, and stirring rate. Following direct-immersion extraction, the analytes were desorbed with methanol and quantified by gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The concentration-dependent calibration curves over a range of 100–900 ng/mL exhibited good linearity (r2 = 0.96–0.99). The fabricated patches provided a simple and cost-effective sampling platform for laboratory-scale applications. This study enabled the evaluation of multiple ketone bodies with different physicochemical properties on a single platform. The environmental sustainability of the method was evaluated using the Analytical Greenness Metric (AGREE, 0.78), the Blue Applicability grade Index (BAGI, 70), and the Carbon Footprint Reduction Index (CaFRI, 88), demonstrating good analytical performance with a reduced environmental footprint. These findings show the potential of the developed glass fiber-based patches as a cost-effective, environmentally sustainable sampling platform for ketone body analysis and provide a foundation for future evaluation in clinically relevant biological matrices. However, future validation in real biological matrices is required before considering this technique for clinical use.

item.title: Preparation and Properties of Superhydrophobic Coatings
item.description:
Abstract
Superhydrophobic coatings possess many exceptional properties; however, their complex preparation processes remain a major barrier to industrial-scale production. In this study, a high-performance superhydrophobic coating was fabricated via a one-step method, in which ammonia was used as the catalyst to modify nano-SiO2 with vinyltriethoxysilane (VTES). The effects of varying dosages of nano-SiO2, VTES, and NH4OH on the contact angle of the resultant coatings were systematically investigated. The optimal coating exhibited outstanding superhydrophobicity, with a static contact angle (CA) of 150.7° and a sliding angle (SA) of 4.8°. The micromorphology and elemental composition of nano-SiO2 before and after modification were characterized by SEM, FTIR, and XPS, and the modification mechanism as well as the origin of superhydrophobicity were elucidated. After 72 h of immersion in tap water, seawater, acidic solution (pH = 2), and alkaline solution (pH = 12), the coating maintained a high CA and a low SA, demonstrating excellent chemical stability. Additionally, the coating was successfully constructed on aluminum, ceramic, silicon wafer, and concrete substrates while retaining its superhydrophobic performance, indicating its wide applicability. This work develops a one-pot, ammonia-catalyzed route for room-temperature-curable coatings prepared via drop coating. Using VTES as the sole silane precursor, the superhydrophobicity of the coating originates from the synergistic effect of vinyl groups and in situ formed micro/nanoscale hierarchical roughness. This fluorine-free strategy features environmental friendliness and cost-effectiveness, holding great potential for large-scale industrial production.

item.title: Antibiotic Microspheres Containing Rutin and Erythromycin: Formulation and Evaluation against Gram-negative Escherichia coli and Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus
item.description:
Abstract
PLGA (poly(d,l-lactide-co-glycolide)) microparticles (MPs) containing the flavonoid glycoside rutin (rutin-loaded PLGA) or the conventional macrolide antibiotic erythromycin (erythromycin-loaded PLGA) were prepared using an oil-in-water (o/w) single-emulsion solvent evaporation method. The MPs were characterized by techniques including particle size analysis, zeta potential, differential scanning calorimetry, and FTIR. Drug loads of 14–33% and encapsulation efficiencies of 33–75% were observed. The antibacterial properties of the biocomposites were examined against two types of bacterial strains: Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and Gram-negative Escherichia coli. The results showed that both the rutin-loaded PLGA and the erythromycin-loaded PLGA MP formulations exhibited significant antibacterial effects against both bacterial strains. The enhanced antibacterial activity of the natural product rutin in the controlled-release formulation reveals the potential for new applications of common compounds in new formulations.

item.title: Pressurized Torrefaction of Distiller’s Grains Using Response Surface Methodology: Process Parameter Optimization and Solid Product Characterization
item.description:
Abstract
Pressurized torrefaction (PT) is regarded as a promising pretreatment method for high-moisture biomass, and its operation parameters have a significant influence on the economy and performance of solid products (biochars). PT of distillers’ grains (DG) was carried out in an autoclave reactor by using response surface methodology. The effects of the operation parameters of initial pressure, moisture, temperature, and residence time on solid yield (SY), higher heating value (HHV), energy yield (EY), and electricity consumption per unit HHV (ECBH) were analyzed. The performances of the three biochars obtained at the maximum EY, optimum operation conditions, and maximum HHV were characterized by proximate and ultimate analyses, N2 adsorption/desorption, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transformed infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The obtained results indicated that temperature had the most significant influence on SY, HHV, and EY, while moisture had the most obvious impact on ECBH. A significant interaction effect between moisture and temperature occurred during the PT of DG, which, along with the initial pressure, led to changes in the system pressure, thereby affecting the performance of the biochars. The biochar obtained at the optimal conditions of 0.1 MPa, 15% moisture, 233 °C, and 60 min exhibited an SY of 65.53%, HHV of 21.78 MJ/kg, EY of 76.45%, and ECBH of 10.24, which confirms the quadratic regression model’s prediction. Compared with raw DG, the fixed carbon and HHV of the three biochars increased by 66%–124% and 12%–35%, while the oxygen content, H/C ratio, and O/C ratio decreased by 25%–59%, 18%–27%, and 34%–69%, respectively. The specific surface area and thermal stability of the biochars improved, but their comprehensive combustion performance slightly decreased as the PT severity increased. These findings could provide an important reference for improving the fuel quality of raw DT through the PT process.

item.title: Controlling the Ligand Spin of Surface-Adsorbed Double-Decker Phthalocyaninato Complexes: Suggestions Based on Theoretical Calculations
item.description:
Abstract
Single-molecule magnetic materials, with potential applications in molecular memory and quantum bits, have been synthesized using ligands that possess electronic spins. Unpaired electrons on ligands are strongly affected by substrate adsorption, and these electrons are transferred to the substrate; however, the mechanism behind this phenomenon remains unclear. To fully leverage the sophisticated molecular design, insight is required into how to mitigate this undesirable substrate-adsorption effect. In this study, the effects of adsorption on unpaired electrons of the ligand were investigated using density functional theory, whereby practical approaches are suggested for controlling the magnetic properties of double-decker phthalocyaninato (MPc2) complexes as representative single-molecule magnetic materials via surface engineering. The key aspect of these approaches is to decrease the orbital correlation between the molecule and substrate in the axial direction perpendicular to the surface. We further demonstrate that large surface coverage of the substrate and insertion of a screening layer, such as graphene, between the molecule and substrate are effective for preserving the electronic spins on the Pc ligands.

item.title: Piezoelectric Biomaterials as Self-Powered Bioelectrical Modulators Enabling Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling for Bone Regeneration
item.description:
Abstract
Under pathological conditions such as metabolic disorders, infections, or tumors, bone tissues exhibit impaired regenerative capacity associated with disrupted bioelectrical signaling. As self-powered bioelectrical modulators, piezoelectric biomaterials can address this challenge by harvesting biomechanical energy from body movements and converting it into bioelectrical stimulation, offering a promising strategy for pathological bone regeneration. Through biomimetic electromechanical regulation, immunomodulation, and metabolic reprogramming, piezoelectric materials actively remodel the microenvironment and promote bone regeneration. This review systematically outlines the common pathological features associated with bone defects under diverse disease conditions. It then discusses the molecular mechanisms through which piezoelectric stimulation regulates biological responses, including mechanotransduction, calcium signaling, immune modulation, and metabolic reprogramming. Finally, we integrate current material design strategies by linking material functional optimization and self-powered activation with electromechanical performance and regenerative outcomes across different pathological conditions. These insights establish a conceptual framework for the rational design of self-powered piezoelectric biomaterials capable of precise and adaptive bioelectrical modulation, providing guidance for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for complex bone defects.

item.title: Experimental Investigation on Stimulated Fracture Network Evolution of Multilayer Radial Wells Fracturing in Shale Oil Reservoir
item.description:
Abstract
Radial well fracturing is promising for enhancing the stimulated reservoir area of continental shale oil as a stimulation technology integrating radial drilling and hydraulic fracturing. In this paper, to clarify the vertical propagation behavior of fractures induced by multilayer radial wells, true triaxial fracturing experiments of Qingshankou continental shale are designed and performed based on similarity criteria. A three-dimensional (3D) fracture reconstruction method based on laser scanning technology is used to quantitatively evaluate the reconstruction area, vertical propagation height, and initiation pressure of fractures under different radial well diameters, lengths, azimuth angles, and in situ stress conditions. The results show that compared with open-hole fracturing and single-layer radial well fracturing, multilayer radial wells fracturing exhibits a stronger ability to control the directional extension of fractures and a larger stimulated reservoir area. Increasing the radial well diameter and length can effectively lower the fracture initiation pressure, improve the steering effect of radial wells on fracture growth, and strengthen the vertical interface penetration of fractures. In addition, the radial well azimuth angle and in situ stress competitively dominate the evolution of the fracture network. Especially for normal fault reservoirs, the combination of a minor azimuth angle and significant horizontal stress difference activates the synergy between multilayer radial wells and in situ stress, which greatly increases the vertical propagation height and reduces fracture complexity. The findings provide crucial theoretical support for revealing the fracture network evolution in multilayer radial wells fracturing and deliver a viable approach to address the challenge of limited vertical stimulation within shale oil reservoirs.

item.title: Shift from Flexible Random Coil to Rigid β-Strand-Rich Conformations Is Associated with Impaired HDL Cholesterol-Acceptor Capacity in Familial Hypercholesterolemia
item.description:
Abstract
Patients with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) exhibit alterations in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) composition and structure, although the functional consequences of these changes have not been fully characterized. Our objectives are to explore the HDL lipid composition, morphology, and structural properties in patients with FH and healthy controls and to investigate their potential association with HDL cholesterol-acceptor capacity. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed no differences in HDL particle size or morphology between groups. In contrast, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed higher total lipid-to-protein, esterified lipid-to-protein, and cholesteryl ester-to-protein ratios in HDL from patients with FH. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further revealed a cholesteryl ester (CE) core phase transition in FH-HDL that was not detected in control HDL, indicating differences in the organization of the HDL lipid core. Analysis of the FTIR amide I band revealed a reduced random-coil content and increased β-strand content in HDL proteins from patients with FH compared with controls. Random-coil content was positively associated with HDL cholesterol-acceptor capacity, whereas the β-strand subcomponent at 1620–1626 cm–1 was inversely associated with cholesterol-acceptor capacity in the overall and FH cohorts. Although cholesterol-acceptor capacity was lower in FH than in controls in unadjusted analysis, this difference was no longer significant after adjustment for age (p = 0.222). After adjustment for age and lipid variables, the inverse association with the β-strand subcomponent was no longer significant, whereas the positive association with random-coil content remained significant in overall and FH cohorts. In conclusion, FH is associated with alterations in HDL lipid organization and protein secondary structure despite preserved particle size and morphology. The persistent association between random-coil content and cholesterol-acceptor capacity suggests a relationship between HDL protein conformational flexibility and cholesterol handling. These exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in independent cohorts and mechanistic studies to determine whether alterations in HDL structural flexibility are related to cholesterol-acceptor capacity in FH.

item.title: Correlation of Senescence-Related Pathways with Ultraweak Photon Emission and Oxidative Stress in Human Epidermal Keratinocytes
item.description:
Abstract
In skin, loss of cellular functions with age impacts overall skin integrity and physiology. Cellular aging in skin keratinocytes disrupts both cell cycle regulation and oxidative stress responses, yet the interaction between these processes remains poorly understood. In the current study, we compared early and late passage normal human keratinocytes (NHKs) using Western blotting and/or immunofluorescence to profile p16INK4a/Rb, p21Cip1, and p53 expression. The response to oxidative stress was measured by ultraweak photon emission (UPE). The late passage NHKs showed an upregulation of p16 and p21, accompanied by a marked reduction in p53 expression. Oxidative stimulation led to a strong UPE signal in late passage cells compared to early passage cells, reflecting increased oxidative reactivity toward chemically generated reactive oxygen species (ROS). These findings suggest that replicative aging in NHKs is likely accompanied by a shift toward a senescence-associated phenotype, marked by elevated cell cycle inhibitors. An increased level of UPE in late passage cells indicates increased susceptibility to ROS-driven damage, which may compromise skin barrier integrity, delay wound healing, and accelerate visible skin aging. This coupling of impaired cell cycle control with exaggerated oxidative reactivity highlights potential molecular targets for interventions aimed at preserving skin function during aging.

item.title: Repeated Laser Exposure Enhances Electrochemical Response in Ag/Laser-Induced Graphene Electrodes with a Hierarchical Assessment of Fabrication Reproducibility
item.description:
Abstract
Laser-induced graphene (LIG) provides a scalable, maskless route to porous carbon electrodes, but variability among independently fabricated devices and batches limits reliable manufacturing. Here, a controlled Ag/LIG workflow was used to examine how a one- to three-pass laser sequence affects material structure, electrochemical response, and fabrication reproducibility. SEM indicated pass-dependent network restructuring within the sampled fields, Raman spectroscopy showed greater but spatially nonuniform graphitic ordering, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated greater sp2 character and modest surface deoxygenation with repeated laser exposure. Three-pass electrodes produced an approximately 2.3-fold higher square-wave voltammetric response than one-pass electrodes in ferri/ferrocyanide solution. Cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy, and direct resistance measurements on representative electrodes showed that the largest resistance decrease occurred between one and two passes, whereas conditional apparent electroactive area continued to increase, with the larger increment occurring between two and three passes; charge-transfer resistance remained comparatively small and showed no systematic dependence on pass number. Reproducibility of the selected three-pass process was evaluated using 18 devices from three fabrication batches and 162 voltammograms: scan-to-scan relative SD was below 0.5%, while device-within-batch and batch relative SDs were 2.6–3.6% and 2.0–4.4%, respectively. These results link controlled multipass processing to staged improvements in electrical transport and electrochemical accessibility and provide a hierarchical framework for quantifying the fabrication reproducibility of porous carbon electrodes.

item.title: Quantifying Macromolecular Transport and Retention Kinetics of Folate-Targeted Polymers in Breast Cancer: A Physics-Informed Differentiable Digital Twin Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate characterization of targeted nanomedicine transport kinetics remains a challenge in cancer therapeutics due to sparse, noisy experimental biodistribution data. Conventional models separate simulation from parameter estimation and often fail to capture the multiphase uptake and prolonged matrix retention of targeted macromolecular carriers within the tumor microenvironment. Here, we present a physics-informed neural network (PINN) architecture serving as a continuous gray-box tool, a differentiable digital twin (DT), to address parameter identifiability challenges in cancer nanomedicine kinetics. The framework integrates a reduced-order phenomenological physical prior with Deep Galerkin Method (DGM) layers, residual-based attention, and self-adaptive loss scaling to ensure optimization stability while preserving structural mass balances. Validated on an ultrasparse, eight-point murine breast cancer biodistribution dataset of folate-targeted poly(styrene-alt-maleic anhydride)–paclitaxel nanoparticles (FA–PSMAC–PTX), the differentiable DT reconstructed continuous concentration profiles with high in-sample fidelity (R2 > 0.98, RMSE ≈ 12 μg mL–1) and predicted withheld time points out of sample (leave-one-time-point-out Rcv2 = 0.74) and resolved hidden transport constants. Information-theoretic comparisons of the mechanistic structures indicated improved parsimony over passive diffusion baselines. Furthermore, the autograd-preserving framework yields instant analytical dose-sensitivity fields (∂Ĉt/∂C0) detailing real-time tumor exposure changes. This framework provides an interpretable method for profiling the real-world kinetics of complex polymer conjugates in solid oncology models, bridging computational data science and rational nanomedicine design.

item.title: Pyrolysis Dechlorination of Sewage Sludge–Fly Ash Co-Hydrothermal Solid Products: Chlorine Distribution, Migration Pathways, and Mechanism
item.description:
Abstract
This study investigated the effects of pyrolysis temperature (500–900 °C) and sewage sludge (SS)/municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (FA) mass ratio (1:0, 4:1, 2:1, 1:1) on thermal dechlorination of cohydrothermal solid-phase products using a fixed-bed pyrolysis system. The distribution of chlorine (Cl) among pyrolytic products was systematically analyzed, and the migration-transformation pathways and dechlorination mechanisms of Cl during pyrolysis were comprehensively explored. The results demonstrate that pyrolysis can effectively facilitate Cl removal from cohydrothermal solid residues. The dechlorination efficiency is primarily governed by pyrolysis temperature and the SS/FA mass ratio; higher temperatures and elevated SS fractions promote Cl volatilization from the solid matrix, achieving a maximum Cl removal rate of 42% under optimized conditions. In pyrolysis residues, interconversion occurs between water-soluble and acid-soluble inorganic Cl. Ca5(PO4)3Cl and Ca3Al2(SiO4)2Cl4 are the dominant acid-soluble Cl-bearing species, and high-temperature crystal evolution dominates the speciation transformation of inorganic Cl. The migration and transformation of Cl are synergistically modulated by inorganic minerals, organic matter, and carbonaceous components via multiple mechanisms, including mineral-induced Cl immobilization, HCl generation and capture, direct volatilization of KCl, and formation of organochlorine compounds. Therefore, pyrolysis is proven to be an effective strategy to enhance dechlorination of SS-FA cohydrothermal solid-phase products. This work provides theoretical support for the resource utilization of chlorine-laden solid wastes.

item.title: Marine Fish-Derived Collagen for Eco-Compatible Cartilage Tissue Engineering
item.description:
Abstract
Marine fish-derived collagen has gained attention as a promising source for collagen extraction for tissue engineering applications. In this study, collagen was isolated from the scales of Asian seabass (Lates calcarifer) using acetic acid and pepsin extraction methods, followed by physicochemical characterization. Sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) revealed characteristic α1, α2, and β chains, while Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) showed characteristic amide bands, supporting the molecular and structural similarity of the extracted collagen to standard type I collagen. The amino acid compositions, thermal stability, and structural organization were evaluated. The extracted collagen was subsequently incorporated into scaffold fabrication using the freeze-drying technique by blending with agarose, chitosan, and gelatin. The resulting scaffold demonstrated successful formation of a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold with porous and sponge-like characteristics. The fabricated scaffolds exhibited pore sizes of 75 to 200 μm, a high water absorption capacity of up to 90%, and a degradation rate of 39% after 4 weeks. Mechanical compression analysis revealed elastic modulus values ranging from 112 to 141 kPa. Furthermore, chondrocytes cultured on the scaffolds for 3 weeks were able to proliferate and grow effectively. These findings suggest that the natural biomaterial-based scaffolds developed in this study were noncytotoxic and capable of supporting chondrocyte proliferation. Importantly, the research also demonstrates the value-added utilization of fish scale waste through collagen extraction for the development of scaffolds with properties suitable for future tissue engineering applications.

item.title: Suppressing Intramolecular C–H Insertion Enables Topochemical Polymerization: Rational Linker Design Controls Nitrene Reactivity in MOF Thin Films
item.description:
Abstract
Azide-based photochemistry enables access to highly reactive nitrene intermediates, yet controlling their reactivity and selectivity remains challenging. We demonstrate that these species can be tamed by generating them from azide precursors that are precisely positioned and oriented. To this end, we tailor linkers and grow surface-mounted metal–organic framework (MOF) thin films (SURMOFs). In azide-functionalized stilbene-based SURMOFs, photogenerated nitrene species undergo rapid intramolecular C–H insertion, effectively suppressing intermolecular reactions. By contrast, replacing the stilbene unit with a tolane-derived linker inhibits this pathway and enables a topochemical reaction that propagates through the crystalline lattice and yields oligomers of up to six units. This strategy affords conjugated backbones composed of azobenzene units linked by acetylene bridges, establishing a previously inaccessible polymer motif that uniquely combines extended π-conjugation with intrinsic photoresponsivity. The structural order, defined orientation, and uniform thickness of SURMOFs studied under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) provide solvent-free conditions for quantitative analysis. A combination of UHV-IRRAS, X-ray diffraction (XRD), mass spectrometry (MS), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) affords molecular-level insight into the reaction mechanism. These results establish a general strategy for redirecting nitrene chemistry from intramolecular quenching to intermolecular coupling via lattice preorganization, enabling spatially resolved topochemical bond formation and solid-state polymerization in reticular materials.

item.title: Water-Free In Situ Incorporation of Starch in Itaconate-Based Photocurable Systems via Oligomer-Mediated Compatibility
item.description:
Abstract
To determine whether the oligomer-forming environment could facilitate starch dispersion, resin-phase stability, and subsequent photocured-network behavior without prefunctionalization, unmodified starch was used in place of conventional postaddition or premodification. The formulations had densities between 1.15 and 1.33 g cm–3 and viscosities between 214 and 470 mPa·s. All of the phase-separation indices were less than 10%. A lower-molecular-weight fraction and a predominantly low-molecular-weight oligomeric population with an apparent Mw of roughly 500–700 g mol–1 were detected by gel permeation chromatography (GPC) of the THF-soluble resin fraction. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) revealed that while reduced-starch formulations exhibited greater viscoelastic relaxation and stronger frequency dependence, rubbery-region moduli and apparent elastically effective chain densities increased with higher glycerol-itaconate and starch fractions. Solvent resistance, morphology, mechanical reinforcement, and tensile strength all showed composition-dependent relationships, as supported by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations. Tensile strengths of roughly 7 MPa were found, while ethanol-insoluble fractions were 87–96% in 72 h extraction. Ultimately, a few formulations were successfully printed with layer heights of 0.05 and 0.10 mm using stereolithography (SLA) with 405 nm UV light. The findings demonstrate a water-free method for controlling the structure, processing, and property balance of an oligomer formation system containing unaltered starch.

item.title: Investigating the Formulation of Agar and Glycerol to Improve Mechanical Performance of Thermal-Compressed Agar Films via Hot Compression Molding
item.description:
Abstract
The transition from traditional solvent casting to hot compression molding at 150 °C and 1000 psi establishes a scalable dry processing framework for fabricating thermoplastic agar Bioplastic films. A constrained four-component mixture design was implemented to evaluate fundamental material interactions, structural synergy, and behavioral boundaries across a bounded compositional space. Formulation variations revealed significant trade-offs between mechanical strength, elasticity, and surface wettability. The high-agar formulation (55/22/15/8 wt %) demonstrated an elevated tensile strength of 10.70 MPa, a tensile modulus of 19.73 MPa, and a hydrophobic contact angle of 101.45°, despite exhibiting a reduced elongation at break of 4.65%. Conversely, balancing agar and glycerol at equal mass ratios (45/45/5/5 wt %) yielded a flexible matrix with 80.95% elongation at break and 3.90 MPa tensile strength, supported by a distinct melting endotherm at 141.0 °C and unified thermal degradation kinetics. Spectroscopic and microstructural analyses demonstrated that divalent calcium ions form ionic cross-links with hydroxyl groups on the agar backbone, lowering O–H stretching wavenumbers from 3307 to 3282 cm–1 and increasing matrix rigidity. However, excessive plasticizer increases matrix free volume, overriding ionic bridging and escalating film swelling up to 204.21%. Surface hydrophobicity is governed by the physical migration of calcium stearate; restricted free volume in low-glycerol networks excludes nonpolar stearate tails onto the film surface, whereas high plasticizer levels accommodate additives internally, causing contact angles to collapse to 17.10°. Strategic management of multicomponent structural cross-linking and plasticization boundaries provides a predictive foundation for engineering high-performance seaweed bioplastics

item.title: Fabrication of Large-Pore Volume Phosphorus-Doped Porous Carbon Spheres Derived from tert -Butyl Alcohol and Formaldehyde for the Removal of Rhodamine B
item.description:
Abstract
Hierarchical carbon materials containing both bimodal mesoporous and macroporous structures have enhanced properties with controlled morphology. In this paper, phosphorus-doped porous carbon microspheres (PMCSs) derived from the carbon deposition reaction were obtained by a novel and feasible template approach at a low temperature range of 300–500 °C, with tert-butyl alcohol and formaldehyde as carbon sources and P-impregnated commercial silica gel as the template, catalyst, and phosphorus source. More importantly, the obtained PMCSs with spherical morphology possess abundant mesopores, high specific surface areas (692 m2g–1), and ultrahollow carbon frameworks (5.83 cm3g–1), as well as phosphorus doping (0.34 wt %) in the carbon matrix. Due to these merits, PMCSs were investigated as adsorbents for the removal of Rhodamine B (RhB) and exhibited excellent adsorption performance (313 mg/g), which is higher than those reported in most previous studies. The current work provides new insights into the rational design of heteroatom-doped porous carbonaceous materials and shows that carbon deposition has the potential to be an effective, low-cost, and scalable route toward the preparation of promising high-performance hierarchical carbon materials in the future.

item.title: All4144, a Cyanobacterial GrpE Homologue, Retains Canonical DnaK-Associated Cochaperone Activity While Its N-Terminal HTH Domain Mediates DNA Binding
item.description:
Abstract
This study characterizes All4144, an unusual GrpE homologue containing a canonical GrpE domain and an additional N-terminal helix-turn-helix (HTH-like) region. The grpE gene (all4144) from Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 was cloned and expressed heterologously in Escherichia coli. To investigate the functional contribution of the N-terminal region, a deletion variant lacking residue 1–67, designated All4144(68–214), was generated. Both full-length All4144 and All4144(68–214) formed homodimers and retained DnaK-associated cochaperone activities, including stimulation of DnaK ATPase activity and enhancement of substrate refolding. In contrast, only full-length All4144 exhibited detectable dsDNA-binding activity, which was abolished following deletion of residues 1–67, indicating a specific contribution of the N-terminal HTH-like region to DNA binding. The N-terminal deletion also reduced the thermal stability of the protein while retaining its overall folded state and DnaK-associated activities. Together, these findings identify All4144 as an unusual GrpE homologue in which a canonical DnaK-associated cochaperone function is coupled with an additional, functionally separable DNA-binding activity mediated by its N-terminal HTH-like region.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights into Cu 2+ Adsorption on an Aminosilane-Functionalized Silica Monolith
item.description:
Abstract
A functionalized silica (SiO2NH2) monolith was prepared through the hydrolysis and co-condensation of tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) and N-[3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl]-ethylenediamine and fabricated into a disc-shaped gel for Cu2+ adsorption. The dried monolith was characterized by ATR-FTIR, 29Si CP/MAS NMR, SEM-EDX, TGA, BET surface analysis, and surface charge measurements. Adsorption studies were conducted at different pH values (2–6) and initial Cu2+ concentrations (10–6–10–1 M), with Cu2+ concentrations determined by atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS). Higher adsorption capacities were obtained at higher pH values, which was attributed primarily to reduced protonation of the amino groups and decreased competition from H+, thereby facilitating interactions between Cu2+ ions and the SiO2NH2 surface. The maximum experimental adsorption capacity reached 460.54 mg g–1 at 0.1 M Cu2+ and pH 4, while complete adsorption was observed at lower Cu2+ concentrations (10–6–10–4 M). Competitive adsorption studies showed that Cd2+ had only a minor effect on Cu2+ uptake, whereas Ni2+ significantly interfered with Cu2+ adsorption, particularly under strongly acidic conditions. Equilibrium adsorption data were evaluated using Langmuir, Freundlich, Temkin, and Sips isotherm models. The Sips model provided the best statistical description of the concentration range of 10–4–10–1 M, accommodating deviations from ideal Langmuir behavior while retaining the high-concentration data. However, because a clear saturation plateau was not reached, the Sips-derived maximum capacities were considered model-dependent limiting parameters. The Freundlich n values close to unity indicated an approximately linear concentration dependence of equilibrium adsorption over the investigated concentration range.
